01 / The need

Every autonomous machine has the same blind spot: the world beyond its sensors.

Onboard perception is bounded by line of sight, weather, obstruction, range, and the position of a single vehicle. The environment itself has no shared memory.

TODAY'S PERCEPTION GAP

The road is passive.
Every vehicle starts from zero.

Cosmic makes the physical environment an active participant in perception—creating shared spatial context before, around, and beyond each vehicle.

01

Line of sight breaks

Buildings, traffic, weather, and distance can hide what matters next.

02

Vehicles sense alone

Each machine rebuilds the same local picture from its own limited position.

03

Context disappears

Without infrastructure, spatial observations are temporary and fragmented.

02 / The Cosmic layer

From radio signals to spatial intelligence.

Distributed roadside nodes observe overlapping regions, preserve the identity and timing of RF observations, and reconstruct a continuously updated model of the world.

STEP 01

Observe together

Geographically distributed nodes sense common space from multiple positions.

STEP 02

Synchronize and resolve

Time, frequency, phase, transmitter, and receiver context remain connected.

STEP 03

Reconstruct the world

Physics-informed and learned methods build persistent 3D spatial hypotheses.

03 / The output

An RF Spatial World Model.

Not another sensor feed. A structured layer of spatial intelligence that independent autonomous, industrial, analytical, and software systems can use.

GEOMETRY

Shape and occupancy

A machine-readable representation of structures, objects, free space, and physical boundaries.

DYNAMICS

Motion and time

Kinematic and temporal state that can evolve as new observations arrive.

TRUST

Confidence and provenance

Uncertainty and observation lineage stay attached to the reconstructed world.

PRIVACY

Non-optical by design

Spatial and semantic understanding without conventional imagery as the primary representation.

Distributed RF nodes→Cosmic reconstruction→Spatial world model→Autonomous systems
